item.title: Candidate named Hitler Mussolini elected mayor in Peru
item.description:
A politician named Hitler Mussolini Simeón Flores has won a mayoral election in Peru, securing 229 votes on a center-left party ticket. Simeón, 45, finished first in Queropalca, a district in Peru’s Huánuco region with a population of just over 730 people. Running for the Ahora Nación (Now Nation) party, he received 34.5% of the 663 valid votes cast in the election. His nearest competitor, Gaspar Benilde Osorio Zambrano of Popular Renewal Peru, received 204 votes, putting Simeón ahead by 25. His victory awaits formal proclamation by the electoral authority. Simeón’s name evokes Adolf Hitler, the leader of Nazi Germany, and Benito Mussolini, Italy’s fascist dictator and Hitler’s wartime ally. According to his candidate declaration, Simeón resigned from the populist right-wing Popular Force party in 2025 before running for Ahora Nación. item.description:
As so-called prediction markets like Kalshi and Polymarket embed themselves in every aspect of our daily lives, from elections to sports and entertainment, concerns have grown about what the explosion of these poorly understood, loosely regulated platforms could mean for regular people and democracy writ large. item.title: Where Are the Iran War Protests?
item.description:
In the immediate aftermath of the 9/11 attacks, a vengeful America was braying for blood. Nine out of 10 Americans approved of attacking Afghanistan. About one-third were comfortable with the prospect of Afghan civilian deaths . Less than a quarter thought the conflict would last more than two years. Hardy bands of protesters took to the streets in New York City, D.C., and elsewhere in a vain attempt to prevent the war. They were called scum and traitors and worse. Americans got the war that most of them wanted — and it was an abject disaster . The invasion of Afghanistan begat conflicts across the world: a sprawling global war that brought death and destruction to Burkina Faso, Cameroon, Iran, Iraq, Libya, Niger, the Philippines, Somalia, Syria, Tunisia, Venezuela, and Yemen, among other locales.
